content:
maria: heads-up — ran a microbatch sweep against chat-streaming vs nonstream completions on rtx-pool-3. short results: streaming p95 stable at mb<=8, p99 jumps at mb>=12. nonstream throughput improves with mb=16 as expected.

samir: can you paste the numbers? on which model and seq-len?

maria: model: llama-13b-q4, mean seq=96, tail seq 512. test load: 300 qps, mix: 70% streaming chat, 30% batch completions. p95/p99: streaming mb=4 -> p95=110ms p99=320ms; mb=8 -> p95=130ms p99=360ms; mb=12 -> p95=160ms p99=980ms (big tail); nonstream mb=16 -> p95=240ms p99=420ms.

linh: that p99 jump screams KV-cache miss + kernel fallback. did you capture kernel selection traces?

maria: yes — attaching inline sample trace:

```
trace_id=trace-7b9
step=attn kernel=attn_fused_opt time_ms=12.4 kv_hit=true
step=kvcache lookup time_ms=2.1
step=matmul kernel=gemm_generic_fallback time_ms=145.7 kv_hit=false
```

maria: when kv_hit=false we hit that generic gemm which balloons latency on the tail.

samir: interesting. sequence-length distribution causing different kernel path? maybe the fused attention supports up to 256 tokens and falls back for >256? but your mean seq=96... why fallback appears only at mb>=12?

devon: microbatch size impacts contention for KV cache memory and eviction patterns. larger mb means more concurrent contexts, more hotset churn, and more KV misses at tail. also larger mb increases queueing for the specialized kernel which then times out to generic.

linh: can we correlate per-request kv_hit rate with mbsize? run a run with instrumentation that records kv_hit boolean per request and kernel choice. add a histogram of kv_hit by mb.

maria: did that: kv_hit_rate by mb: mb=4 -> 98.6%; mb=8 -> 97.2%; mb=12 -> 88.9%; mb=16 -> 74.5%. so yes, big drop after 8.

infra-bot: perf-canary: canary deploy 2026-03-17T11:05 rolled to rtx-pool-3 at 2965432005 (sha: d23f8).

maria: the regression correlated with that canary deploy (we see baseline p99 ~360 then post-deploy spike to ~980).

samir: two avenues: 1) tweak kernel selector to prefer fused path even when mb groups larger (if safe), 2) change batching heuristics / separate pools for streaming vs nonstream so streaming keeps lower mb. 3) try KV prefetch for tail contexts.

linh: kernel-selector: the selector currently picks kernel based on max_seq_in_batch and per-model capability flags. When mb increases, combined max_seq in microbatch occasionally leaps (because of tail inputs) causing fallback. We could change to per-request kernel decision instead of per-batch OR cap microbatching to avoid mixing very long sequences into same microbatch.

devon: i'd prefer split pools: small-mb pool with reserved slots for streaming (mb cap 8) and a bulk pool for nonstream (mb up to 32). That reduces cross-traffic and KV churn. downside: utilization hit unless autoscale/burst is tuned.

maria: tried split pools in a quick sim: streaming p99 drops to 380 with mb cap 8 and kv_hit ~97.8; nonstream throughput slightly lower but acceptable.

samir: what about KV prefetch? maybe when request starts streaming we can pre-warm kv for expected continuation lengths. how would that be configured?

linh: there's an experimental flag: `kv_prefetch_window=64` and `kv_prefetch=true`. set on request metadata. It instructs runtime to prefetch expected next 64 tokens' KV into GPU before handing off to fused kernel. Could mitigate misses for long tails.

maria: quick test with kv_prefetch=true, mb=12: p99 dropped from 980 -> 430, kv_hit_rate up to 95.6. still worse than mb<=8 but much better.

devon: nice. cost tradeoff though — prefetch does extra compute and memory. need cost model: prefetch per-request token-prefetch cost vs p99 reduction.

samir: could also add hysteresis to batch formation: don't let a long seq join an existing microbatch if it would push the batch into fallback kernel; start a new microbatch or route it to dedicated long-seq lane. That avoids penalizing short ones.

maria: implemented a quick heuristic: if incoming seq > batch_mean + 2*stddev then hold and create separate microbatch. result: p99 for streaming mb=12 -> 410, kv_hit 95.1, small QPS drop 2.3%.

linh: sounds promising. production rollout plan? canary on single pool, monitor p99, kv_hit, and utilization. also add a regression alert for deploy-bot to auto-roll if p99 increase > 20% over baseline.

deploy-bot: canary started for heuristic-split (sha: a1b2c3) on rtx-pool-3 at 2965432120.

maria: rolling the prefetch + batch-hysteresis to canary. will post results in 30m. thanks team. :thumbsup:

linh: one more note — document experimental config flags in README: `kv_prefetch`, `mb_split_threshold`, `batch_hysteresis_std_multiplier`. makes it easier for SRE to tune per-customer.

samir: agreed. also add a dashboard tile showing kernel_fallback_rate over time and per-mb histogram. that was the smoking gun here.

maria: ack. I'll file a follow-up ticket with numbers and the canary link.
